newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech lower house approves energy VAT increase.
newsitem.headline: Czech lower house approves energy VAT increase.

text.p: The lower house of Czech parliament approved on Tuesday a government plan to increase the value added tax on energy sources to 22 percent from five percent, the parliamentary press department told Reuters.
The plan calls for the increase to take effect at the beginning of next year.
The tax hikes on electricity, gas and fuels, were seen as a way for the government to slow aggregate demand while augmenting revenue sources.
It comes alongside other deregulation steps which many economists have expected.

The government accelerated its deregulation of state-controlled rents this month. The rent rises averaged about 50 percent nationwide, but were higher in larger cities, such as Prague where rents jumped as high as 100 percent.
